note: Phase 0 writing sample. Scene facts are paraphrased story events for the opening stretch, standing in for the scene dossiers the new pipeline will build from subtitles and clips.

scenes.shows: A wounded man in a soaked suit runs through rainy New York streets at night, checking a clock.
He was declared excommunicado for killing a crime-lord member on hotel grounds; a $14 million bounty goes live in one hour.
In a public library he retrieves a hidden book holding a medallion and a crucifix. A giant hitman blocks the aisle.
The giant overpowers him. He grabs a heavy book from the shelf and beats the man down with it.
Bleeding, he reaches an underground doctor who must stop treating him the moment the clock strikes six.
The clock strikes. The doctor stops. He finishes stitching himself, then asks to be shot in the shoulder to keep his cover.
Out on the street, phones buzz everywhere. Every stranger turns to look at him.

rules: Open on the most intense visible moment, not on background.
Present tense, plain spoken English, short sentences, concrete nouns and verbs.
Each scene's narration must fit its seconds at about 3.3 words per second, leaving room for the listed dialogue.
Use cause and effect: but, so, then. No filler such as 'in this movie' or 'little did he know'.
End so the last line flows back into the opening shot (Shorts loop).
